# Frozen revision 9 rhythm buses

These compact JSON fingerprints come from the unchanged accepted `session_render.render_song`, not a second implementation of its filter/gain equations. All cases end before the original rhythm handoff fade, and the raw tonal capture precedes any duration-dependent fade.

`rhythm-prefix` contains the unchanged accepted 21 tonal note-ons before eight seconds and 42 rhythm note-ons before 12 seconds, with 13 seconds of output at the accepted song energy. The two five-second controls share 22 synthetic events and use energy zero/one. Each frame has nine Float32 values: guitar left/right, piano left/right, unducked bass left/right, processed drums left/right, and mono duck. Float32 samples are not final mastered audio. Future harmonic processing must retain the original `(tonal + bass) * duck + drums` grouping. The manifest retains full original Float32 SHA256s, exact candidate sizes, per-channel peak/RMS, and deterministic waveform probes near event starts, note endpoints, duck endpoints, and regularly spaced frames. Swift tests use these fingerprints as a compact local gate. The Python verifier regenerates all three full waveforms through the original function and compares every native sample; the fingerprints alone do not establish waveform parity. The original PCM hashes record the freezing platform and are reported beside regenerated hashes, since harmless platform floating-point differences can change a hash. Reproduction and native acceptance use predeclared maximum error `1e-5` and RMS error `1e-6`; duck uses `1e-7` and `1e-8` and exact attack/end assertions. Duck returns exactly to one at 8,960 frames after the latest kick, including a silent kick; overlapping envelopes use their minimum.
